posts.post: More than 170,000 people in Canada have signed a petition calling to expel the U.S. ambassador. According to Al Jazeera, the House of Commons will discuss the petition, which reflects growing discontent with policies from President Trump.
Moroccan security forces in Fnideq have intensified operations to stop migrants attempting to cross into the Spanish enclave of Ceuta, Al Jazeera reports.
Indiana, Illinois, and neighboring Midwestern states are preparing for additional heavy flooding this weekend, with Indiana seeking federal assistance, according to NPR.
At least 47 people have died following a magnitude 7.7 earthquake in eastern Indonesia. BBC News reports that search and rescue teams are working to find survivors on the island of Flores.
Australia's Labor party is navigating a challenging stance on immigration as it attempts to retain suburban and regional seats against a rising One Nation, The Guardian reports.
Attention is increasingly turning to Australia's history of blackbirding, the forced or coerced migration of Pacific Islanders for labor that enriched early colonists, according to The Guardian.
Unethical paper mills allowing authors to purchase published, fraudulent research have expanded rapidly in recent years, compromising medical research and scientific integrity, reports The Guardian.
Under a new agreement in Australia involving platforms like Uber Eats and DoorDash, gig economy delivery drivers are set to receive a minimum wage, according to The Guardian.

A 55.6-meter statue of the Virgin Mary, the tallest in Europe, has been unveiled in a small Polish village during a ceremony featuring Mass, music, and rose petals dropped from helicopters, Euronews reports.

Family members of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln have criticized President Trump's comments calling their deployment not nearly long enough, describing his remarks and onboard conditions as shameful, NPR reports.

Lebanon's president stated that recent Israeli air strikes killing 11 people send a clear message regarding negotiations, while Hezbollah warned the attacks will receive an appropriate response, according to Euronews.
Authoritarian right-wing leaders in Latin America aligned with Trump are forging closer diplomatic ties with Israel despite its growing international isolation, reports DW.
A powerful magnitude 7.7 earthquake has struck eastern Indonesia, killing at least 47 people. Search and rescue operations are currently underway to find survivors on the island of Flores.

Lebanon's president stated that recent Israeli strikes resulting in 11 deaths send a clear message regarding ongoing negotiations. Meanwhile, Hezbollah warned that the latest attacks will be met with an appropriate response.

Families of sailors aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln are criticizing President Trump after he described the ship's deployment as not nearly long enough. Relatives expressed concern over dire conditions on board and called his remarks shameful.
Cleanup operations are underway along 12 kilometers of coastline in Oman after an oil spill from a grounded Russian tanker reached the shore.
Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky confirmed strikes on industrial infrastructure in Russia's Samara region, targeting both a rocket plant and an air base.
As military actions in Gaza and the West Bank leave Israel increasingly isolated globally, right-wing political leaders in Latin America are forging stronger strategic ties with the country.

With ongoing conflicts in Ukraine and Iran shifting global warfare dynamics, military analysts are looking at whether China could adapt blockade tactics similar to those used in the Strait of Hormuz around Taiwan.
The USS Washington is expected to relieve the USS Lincoln in the Middle East following reports of harsh conditions for crew members aboard the Lincoln.

Ukraine launched targeted strikes against a rocket and space center in Russia's Samara region, while also hitting the Savasleyka air base and an oil facility in Ust-Luga, according to President Zelenskyy.
Zambia has resumed its election vote count after a temporary nationwide pause caused by reports of stolen ballots and attacks on polling staff.

Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has warned Egypt that food exports are threatened by Russian strikes in the Black Sea. Meanwhile, Russia has dismissed the idea of a Black Sea ceasefire.

Source: The Guardian
